title: Setup: Four-Step Gauss Sum QR Pathway
content:
The header establishes where this file fits in the Gauss sum QR proof:
- Step 1: Define τ = gaussSum χ ψ
- Step 2: τ² = χ(-1)·p [proved in OQ01OQ01OQ01.lean]
- Step 3: τ^q = χ(q)·τ [THIS FILE]
- Step 4: Comparing τ^q two ways gives QR

The imports are specific: `GaussSum`, `LegendreSymbol.Basic`, `QuadraticChar.Basic`. The `variable {p q : ℕ} [hp : Fact p.Prime] [hq : Fact q.Prime]` makes p, q implicit primes threaded through all instances.
mathContext: $\tau = \mathrm{gaussSum}(\chi, \psi) = \sum_{a \in \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}} \chi(a)\psi(a)$, where $\chi$ is quadratic (Legendre symbol) and $\psi$ additive.

title: Auxiliary: Invertibility of q mod p
content:
The private lemma `q_isUnit_in_ZMod_p` establishes IsUnit(q : ZMod p) for distinct primes p ≠ q.

Proof: `ZMod.isUnit_prime_iff_not_dvd` gives IsUnit(q : ZMod p) ↔ ¬(q ∣ p). Since p is prime, q ∣ p implies q = 1 or q = p — both contradicted by `hq.out.one_lt` and `hpq`.

title: The Frobenius Step: τ^q = χ(q)·τ
content:
The central theorem — one line: `hχ.gaussSum_frob q (q_isUnit_in_ZMod_p hpq) ψ`.

Mathematical content:
1. **Freshman's dream**: (Σ χ(a)ψ(a))^q = Σ (χ(a)ψ(a))^q = Σ χ(a)^q ψ(a)^q (ring hom in char q)
2. **χ^q = χ**: χ(a) ∈ {0,±1}, and (-1)^q = -1 in char q, so χ(a)^q = χ(a)
3. **ψ(a)^q = ψ(qa)**: additive character identity
4. **Reparametrize**: Σ_a χ(a)ψ(qa) = χ(q)·Σ_b χ(b)ψ(b) (substitute b=qa, bijection since q is a unit)

Result: τ^q = χ(q)·τ.

title: Combining Steps 2 and 3: Key QR Identity
content:
Theorem `qr_via_frobenius` takes the hypothesis `hτ_sq : gaussSum χ ψ ^ 2 = χ (-1) * Fintype.card (ZMod p)` (Step 2) and derives (χ(-1)·p)^{(q-1)/2} = χ(q).

Argument:
- τ^q = τ·(τ²)^{(q-1)/2} = τ·(χ(-1)·p)^{(q-1)/2} (exponent arithmetic + hypothesis)
- τ^q = χ(q)·τ (Frobenius step)
- Equating: (χ(-1)·p)^{(q-1)/2} = χ(q)

Lean uses `Char.card_pow_char_pow`. The `simpa [pow_one]` handles the n=1 special case.

title: QR Identity in ZMod q: Encoding QR via Euler's Criterion
content:
The main theorem `qr_gauss_sums_identity`: for distinct odd primes p ≠ q and nontrivial quadratic χ,

    (χ(-1) · Fintype.card (ZMod p))^(Fintype.card (ZMod q) / 2) = χ(Fintype.card (ZMod q))

Using Fintype.card (ZMod n) = n, this reads (χ(-1)·p)^{(q-1)/2} = χ(q) in ZMod q.

**This is QR**: Euler's criterion gives a^{(q-1)/2} ≡ (a/q) mod q. With χ(-1) = (-1/p) = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} and p^{(q-1)/2} ≡ (p/q): the left side is (-1/p)·(p/q); the right is (q/p). So (p/q)(q/p) = (-1)^{((p-1)/2)·((q-1)/2)} — QR.

Proved via `Char.card_pow_card` with `rw [ZMod.ringChar_zmod_n]` to handle coercions.

title: Worked Examples: (5,3), (7,5), (11,7)
content:
Three `example` declarations exhibit the abstract theorems on concrete prime pairs:

• **(p=5, q=3)** in any char-3 field: τ^3 = χ₅(3)·τ. Discharged by `frobenius_step χ hχ ψ (by norm_num)` — `norm_num` certifies the side-condition `5 ≠ 3`.
• **(p=7, q=5)** in any char-5 field: τ^5 = χ₇(5)·τ. Same shape.
• **(p=11, q=7)** in ZMod 7: (χ₁₁(-1)·11)^3 = χ₁₁(7). The QR cross-check: 11 ≡ 4 (mod 7) makes (11/7)=1; 11 ≡ 3 (mod 4) makes (-1/11)=-1; QR predicts (11/7)·(7/11) = (-1)^{((11-1)/2)·((7-1)/2)} = (-1)^{5·3} = -1, matching (-1)·(7/11) = (7/11) = ?... resolvable to -1.

Four `private instance factPrime{3,5,7,11}` declarations (lines 172-175) supply the `[Fact p.Prime]` instances that the variable block depends on; `decide` is enough since the primes are concrete numerals.

title: Part IV-V: Complete Pathway and Concrete Verifications
content:
**gauss_qr_pathway_complete**: Existential summary ∃ result = χ(q) = (χ(-1)·p)^{(q-1)/2}. The `⟨_, symm, rfl⟩` proof documents the connection.

**Three concrete examples**:
- (p=5,q=3): In char 3, (gaussSum χ₅ ψ)³ = χ₅(3)·(gaussSum χ₅ ψ)
- (p=7,q=5): In char 5, similar
- (p=11,q=7): QR identity (χ₁₁(-1)·11)³ = χ₁₁(7) in ZMod 7

All proved by `frobenius_step/qr_gauss_sums_identity χ ... (by norm_num)`.

The docstring for p=11,q=7 computes: 11 ≡ 4 mod 7 → (11/7)=1; (-1/11)=-1 (since 11≡3 mod 4); QR: (11/7)(7/11) = (-1)^{5·3} = -1 ✓.
